The Prophet ﷺ said the one who gets it right has two rewards.
Even the one who errs in it gets one reward.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "If a judge strives and gets it right he has two rewards, and if he strives and errs he has one reward."

clues: It is a quality of the heart.
It goes together with taking the means.
The Qur'an says Allah loves those who have it.
Whoever has it in Allah, He is enough for them.
It means trusting in Allah.
medium.explain: Allah says, "Whoever puts his trust in Allah, He will suffice him," and "Allah loves those who put their trust in Him."

clues: It is a quality of the believer.
It is shown with the heart, the tongue and actions.
Allah promises more to those who show it.
Few of Allah's servants truly have it.
It means gratitude.
medium.explain: Allah says, "If you are grateful, I will surely increase you."

clues: It is a quality of character.
It holds a person back from shameful things.
The Prophet ﷺ had more of it than a girl behind her curtain.
It is one of the branches of faith.
It means modesty or shyness.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "Faith has over sixty branches, and haya' is a branch of faith."

clues: It is a sin of the tongue.
It is done when the person is not present.
It is saying something true that they would dislike.
The Qur'an compares it to eating a dead brother's flesh.
It means backbiting.
medium.explain: Allah says, "Do not backbite one another. Would one of you like to eat the flesh of his dead brother?"

clues: It is a disease of the heart.
It is wishing that someone loses a blessing.
The Prophet ﷺ said, "Do not be jealous of one another."
Surah Al-Falaq seeks refuge from it.
It means envy.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Falaq ends with seeking refuge "from the evil of the envier when he envies."

clues: It is a disease of the heart.
It spoils good deeds.
It is doing good deeds to be seen and praised by people.
Surah Al-Ma'un warns those who pray to be seen.
It means showing off.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Ma'un warns those who are heedless of their prayer, "those who want to be seen."

clues: It is a disease of the heart.
It was the sin of Iblis.
The Prophet ﷺ defined it as rejecting the truth and looking down on people.
No one with an atom's weight of it will enter Paradise.
It means arrogance.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said no one with an atom's weight of pride in his heart will enter Paradise, and explained pride as rejecting truth and looking down on people.

clues: It is a serious sin of the heart.
Outwardly a person shows faith but hides disbelief.
A whole surah is named after the people who have it.
One of its signs is lying when speaking.
It means hypocrisy.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said the signs of a hypocrite are three: when he speaks he lies, when he promises he breaks it, and when trusted he betrays.

clues: It is something every person is born with.
It is mentioned in Surah Ar-Rum.
It is the natural disposition Allah created people on.
The Prophet ﷺ said parents may change it.
It means the natural state.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said every child is born upon the fitrah, then his parents make him a Jew, a Christian or a Magian.

clues: It is part of the Day of Judgement.
It happens only with Allah's permission.
Ayat al-Kursi mentions it.
The Prophet ﷺ will be given the greatest one.
It means intercession.
medium.explain: Ayat al-Kursi asks, "Who is there that can intercede with Him except by His permission?"

clues: It is part of the Day of Judgement.
It belongs to the Prophet ﷺ.
Its water is whiter than milk.
Whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty again.
It is the Prophet's basin.
medium.explain: The Prophet ﷺ described his basin: its water whiter than milk, its smell better than musk, and whoever drinks from it will never thirst again.

clues: It is one of three things explained in a single well-known hadith.
That hadith is narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab.
In it, Jibril came in the form of a man and asked questions.
It was the third thing he asked about, after Islam and Iman.
It was defined as worshipping Allah as though you see Him.
hard.explain: In the Hadith of Jibril, the Prophet ﷺ defined ihsan as worshipping Allah as though you see Him, and if you do not see Him, knowing that He sees you. The same hadith defines Islam and Iman. It is recorded in Sahih Muslim and Sahih al-Bukhari.

clues: It was a written agreement.
It was concluded with the Quraysh.
It happened in 6 AH, outside Makkah.
Its terms looked unfavourable to the Muslims at the time.
Surah Al-Fath refers to it as a clear victory.
hard.explain: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah (6 AH / 628 CE) established a ten-year truce with the Quraysh. Though its terms appeared disadvantageous, the peace it created allowed rapid growth, and Surah Al-Fath describes it as a manifest victory.

clues: It was a defensive engagement at Madinah.
A confederacy of tribes besieged the city.
It is also known by another name referring to that alliance.
A defensive earthwork was dug around part of the city.
The suggestion to dig it is attributed to Salman al-Farisi.
hard.explain: The Battle of Khandaq (the Trench), 5 AH, is also called the Battle of al-Ahzab (the Confederates). A trench was dug around the exposed side of Madinah — a tactic attributed to Salman al-Farisi — and the siege failed without a pitched battle.

clues: It is the name given to a particular year.
It falls in the Makkan period, before the Hijrah.
It is named for grief.
Two people close to the Prophet ﷺ died in it.
They were Khadijah and Abu Talib.
hard.explain: The Year of Sorrow (Am al-Huzn), around 619 CE, is so called because the Prophet ﷺ lost both his wife Khadijah and his uncle Abu Talib within a short period, removing his closest support in Makkah.

clues: It was delivered in the final year of the Prophet's life.
It was given during a pilgrimage.
It was addressed to a very large gathering.
It affirmed the sanctity of life, property and honour.
It stated that no Arab has superiority over a non-Arab except by taqwa.
hard.explain: The Farewell Sermon was delivered during the Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH. Among its themes were the sanctity of life and property, the rights of women, the abolition of pre-Islamic blood feuds and usury, and the equality of people regardless of lineage.

clues: It was a pledge of allegiance.
It took place in 6 AH.
It happened outside Makkah, before a treaty was signed.
It was given beneath a tree.
The Qur'an states that Allah was pleased with the believers who gave it.
hard.explain: The Pledge of Ridwan was given beneath a tree at Hudaybiyyah, when a rumour reached the Muslims that Uthman had been killed. Surah Al-Fath refers to Allah being pleased with the believers who pledged under the tree.

clues: It was a formal document.
It dates from very early in the Madinan period.
It was not an agreement with the Quraysh.
It set out relations between the groups living in one city.
It covered the Muhajirun, the Ansar and the Jewish tribes of Madinah.
hard.explain: The Constitution of Madinah was drawn up shortly after the Hijrah, defining the rights and obligations of the Muhajirun, the Ansar and the Jewish tribes as a single community for purposes of defence and mutual obligation.

clues: They were pledges of allegiance.
They took place before the Hijrah.
They were given during the pilgrimage season.
They were given by people from Yathrib, not Makkah.
They prepared the way for the migration to Madinah.
hard.explain: The two Pledges of Aqabah were given by groups from Yathrib during the pilgrimage season in the years before the Hijrah. They established the support base that made the migration to Madinah possible.

clues: It was the first major battle of the Madinan period.
It took place in Ramadan.
The Muslims were heavily outnumbered.
The Qur'an refers to it as the day of distinction, Yawm al-Furqan.
It was fought in 2 AH.
hard.explain: Badr, fought in Ramadan of 2 AH, was the first major engagement between the Muslims of Madinah and the Quraysh. The Qur'an calls it Yawm al-Furqan, the Day of Distinction.

clues: It was fought near a mountain outside Madinah.
It took place the year after a major victory.
A group of archers left their assigned position.
The Prophet ﷺ was wounded during it.
Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib was killed in it.
hard.explain: Uhud, 3 AH, followed Badr. The withdrawal of archers from the hill they had been ordered to hold turned the course of the battle, and Hamza, the Prophet's uncle, was among those killed.

clues: It happened on the same night as another famous event.
It followed the journey to Jerusalem.
It involved rising upward.
The five daily prayers were prescribed during it.
It was the ascension through the heavens.
hard.explain: The Mi'raj is the ascension that followed the Isra on the same night. It is during this that the five daily prayers were prescribed, after an initial command of fifty.

clues: It is a Madinan surah.
It is named for a victory.
It was revealed in connection with a specific episode.
That episode was an agreement many Muslims found disappointing at the time.
It refers to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah as a manifest victory.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Fath (48) was revealed in connection with the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, describing it as a manifest victory despite its terms appearing unfavourable to the Muslims at the time.

clues: It is the name of a particular year.
It precedes the Prophet's mission.
It is traditionally placed around the year of his birth.
An army marched on Makkah and failed.
Surah Al-Fil refers to it.
hard.explain: The Year of the Elephant is traditionally placed around the Prophet's birth, about 570 CE. Surah Al-Fil refers to the destruction of the army that advanced on Makkah with an elephant.

clues: It is the name given to a year late in the Prophet's life.
It followed the conquest of Makkah.
It is usually dated to 9 AH.
It is named for groups who travelled to Madinah.
Tribes came from across Arabia to accept Islam.
hard.explain: The Year of Delegations, usually placed at 9 AH, is so called because tribes from across Arabia sent delegations to Madinah to accept Islam following the conquest of Makkah.

clues: It was fought outside the Arabian heartland.
It took place in 8 AH, before the conquest of Makkah.
Three appointed commanders were killed in succession.
Khalid ibn al-Walid took command and withdrew the force.
Zayd ibn Harithah and Ja'far ibn Abi Talib were among those killed.
hard.explain: Mu'tah, 8 AH, was fought near the Byzantine frontier. Zayd ibn Harithah, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Rawahah were killed in succession, after which Khalid ibn al-Walid took command and extracted the army.

clues: It took place in 9 AH.
It was undertaken in severe heat and hardship.
It was the last major expedition the Prophet ﷺ led in person.
No battle was actually fought.
Three companions who stayed behind were boycotted until their repentance was accepted.
hard.explain: Tabuk, 9 AH, was undertaken in great heat and difficulty and ended without fighting. Surah At-Tawbah addresses those who stayed behind, including the three whose repentance was eventually accepted.

clues: It was fought in 8 AH.
It came very shortly after a major and peaceful success.
The Muslim force was unusually large this time.
Its opening moments went badly despite that advantage.
The Qur'an notes that their numbers pleased them but availed them nothing.
hard.explain: Hunayn followed soon after the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH. Surah At-Tawbah mentions that the Muslims' large numbers pleased them but were of no avail at first, before the situation was retrieved.

clues: It is a Makkan surah.
Its opening verses have a special status.
Those verses were revealed at the cave of Hira.
They were the very first revelation.
They begin with the command: Read.
hard.explain: The first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq (96) were the first revelation, received at the cave of Hira, beginning with the command 'Iqra' — Read.

clues: It is an institution, not an act of worship.
It developed in the early Islamic state.
It dealt with resources rather than law.
It handled revenue and its distribution.
It was the public treasury.
hard.explain: Bayt al-Mal was the public treasury of the early Islamic state, responsible for collecting and distributing public revenues including zakat and other income.

clues: It is a single well-known narration.
It takes the form of questions and answers.
A stranger arrived whom nobody recognised.
He asked about three things in turn.
Those three were Islam, Iman and Ihsan.
hard.explain: In the Hadith of Jibril, narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, the angel Jibril came in human form and questioned the Prophet ﷺ about Islam, Iman and Ihsan, and the signs of the Hour. It is recorded in Sahih Muslim and Sahih al-Bukhari.

clues: It is a very short surah, three ayahs.
It is placed near the end of the mushaf.
It is widely held to be among the last revealed.
It speaks of people entering the religion in crowds.
It mentions the help of Allah and the victory having come.
hard.explain: Surah An-Nasr (110) has three ayahs and is widely regarded as among the last surahs revealed. It speaks of the help of Allah and of people entering the religion in multitudes.

clues: It took place in 7 AH.
It followed closely on a treaty.
It concerned a set of fortified settlements north of Madinah.
Ali ibn Abi Talib was given the banner.
The settlements were taken after a siege.
hard.explain: Khaybar, 7 AH, followed the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. The fortified oasis settlements north of Madinah were taken after a siege, with Ali ibn Abi Talib given the banner.

clues: It was a pledge given before the Hijrah.
It was given by a small group from Yathrib.
It is sometimes called the pledge of the women.
Its terms concerned conduct, not warfare.
Mus'ab ibn Umayr was sent back with them to teach.
hard.explain: The first Pledge of Aqabah committed a small group from Yathrib to belief and to abstaining from specified wrongs, without any undertaking to fight. Mus'ab ibn Umayr returned with them as a teacher.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of 129 ayahs.
It is the ninth surah.
It is the only surah not opened by the Basmalah.
It deals with treaties and with those who stayed behind.
Its themes connect closely with the expedition to Tabuk.
hard.explain: Surah At-Tawbah (9) is the only surah that does not begin with the Basmalah. Much of it addresses the aftermath of Tabuk and the conduct of those who did not join it.

clues: It concerns the written text of the Qur'an.
It took place very shortly after the Prophet's passing.
It was prompted by the deaths of many memorisers in battle.
Umar proposed it and Zayd ibn Thabit carried it out.
It gathered the Qur'an into a single written collection.
hard.explain: After many huffaz were killed at the Battle of Yamamah, Umar urged Abu Bakr to have the Qur'an gathered into one written collection, a task entrusted to Zayd ibn Thabit. Uthman's later work standardised and distributed copies.

clues: It concerns the written text of the Qur'an.
It happened about twenty years after the Prophet's passing.
It was prompted by differences arising in distant regions.
Official copies were produced and sent to the major centres.
Zayd ibn Thabit was again central to the work.
hard.explain: Uthman had standard copies prepared and sent to the main centres of the expanding state, in response to differences in recitation emerging among new Muslims in distant regions.

clues: It was fought after the Prophet's passing.
It took place during the caliphate of Abu Bakr.
It was part of the Ridda campaigns.
Many memorisers of the Qur'an were killed in it.
It prompted the gathering of the Qur'an into one collection.
hard.explain: Yamamah, fought during Abu Bakr's caliphate against the forces of Musaylimah, cost the lives of many huffaz — which directly prompted the written compilation of the Qur'an.

clues: It was fought during the Rashidun period.
It was fought against the Byzantines.
It took place near a river in the Levant.
Khalid ibn al-Walid played a decisive role.
It opened the way to Muslim control of Syria.
hard.explain: Yarmuk, fought around 15 AH against the Byzantines, was decisive in bringing Syria under Muslim control. Khalid ibn al-Walid's command is widely credited for the outcome.

clues: It was fought during Umar's caliphate.
It was fought against the Sasanian empire, not the Byzantines.
It took place in Iraq.
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas commanded the Muslim force.
It opened the way into Persia.
hard.explain: Qadisiyyah, fought in Iraq under the command of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas during Umar's caliphate, was decisive against the Sasanian empire.

clues: They were a group in Madinah.
They were companions of the Prophet ﷺ.
They had no homes of their own.
They lived on a shaded platform attached to the mosque.
They devoted themselves to learning and worship.
hard.explain: The Ashab al-Suffah were poor companions who lived on a raised, shaded platform at the Prophet's Mosque, devoting themselves to learning. Abu Hurayrah was among them.

clues: The term refers to a group connected to the Prophet ﷺ.
It is not defined by city of origin.
It is mentioned in Surah Al-Ahzab.
Its exact scope is discussed by scholars.
It means the people of the household.
hard.explain: Ahl al-Bayt refers to the household of the Prophet ﷺ, mentioned in Surah Al-Ahzab 33:33. Scholars differ on precisely whom the term encompasses.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of eighteen ayahs.
Its subject is conduct between people.
It addresses how to behave towards the Prophet ﷺ.
It forbids mockery, suspicion and backbiting.
It states that the most honoured are the most God-fearing.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Hujurat (49) sets out norms of conduct: verifying news, reconciling disputes, avoiding mockery, suspicion and backbiting, and the principle that honour lies in taqwa, not lineage.

clues: It is a field within Qur'anic studies.
It concerns context rather than wording.
It records the circumstances in which verses came down.
It helps clarify the intent of particular passages.
It is known in Arabic as asbab al-nuzul.
hard.explain: Asbab al-nuzul records the circumstances in which particular verses were revealed. It assists interpretation, though scholars caution that a verse's ruling is not limited to its occasion.

clues: It was an agreement made in Makkah.
It was made before the Prophet's mission began.
He took part in it as a young man.
It was a pact among clans to aid the wronged.
He later said he would still answer such a call in Islam.
hard.explain: Hilf al-Fudul was a pre-Islamic pact among Makkan clans to support anyone wronged in the city. The Prophet ﷺ participated in his youth and later spoke approvingly of it.

clues: It took place in Makkah before the Hijrah.
It was directed at two clans of the Quraysh.
It lasted roughly three years.
It cut off trade and marriage with them.
Its terms were written and posted in the Ka'bah.
hard.explain: The Quraysh imposed a boycott on Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib for roughly three years, its terms written on a document hung in the Ka'bah. The hardship it caused preceded the Year of Sorrow.

clues: It was a journey undertaken from Makkah.
It took place in the late Makkan period.
Its purpose was to seek support from another town.
The Prophet ﷺ was rejected and driven out.
He returned saying he complained of his weakness only to Allah.
hard.explain: After the Year of Sorrow, the Prophet ﷺ travelled to Ta'if seeking support and was rejected and pelted. The episode is remembered particularly for his supplication on the return journey.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of twenty-four ayahs.
Its name refers to a gathering or exile.
It praises the Ansar for preferring others over themselves.
It warns against being like those who forgot Allah.
Its final three verses enumerate names of Allah.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Hashr (59) closes with three verses enumerating many of the names and attributes of Allah, and earlier praises the Ansar for preferring others over themselves despite their own need.

clues: It is a concept in Qur'anic and legal study.
It concerns rulings over time.
It applies within the period of revelation.
Scholars differ considerably over its extent.
It is the abrogation of an earlier ruling by a later one.
hard.explain: Naskh is the abrogation of an earlier ruling by a later revelation. Its existence is broadly accepted, but scholars differ substantially over how many verses it affects.

clues: It is one of the sources of Islamic law.
It ranks after the Qur'an and the Sunnah.
It is not individual reasoning.
It concerns the position of the scholars collectively.
It is consensus.
hard.explain: Ijma is the consensus of qualified scholars, conventionally the third source of law after the Qur'an and Sunnah. Qiyas, analogical reasoning, is usually listed fourth.

clues: It is one of the sources of Islamic law.
It is conventionally listed fourth.
It is used when no direct text addresses a matter.
It extends an existing ruling to a new case.
It works by identifying a shared underlying cause.
hard.explain: Qiyas is analogical reasoning: extending a ruling from a case addressed by the texts to a new case sharing the same effective cause ('illah). The Zahiri school rejected it.

clues: It is a very short Makkan surah.
It has three ayahs.
It opens with an oath.
It states that mankind is in loss, with exceptions.
Al-Shafi'i said that if people reflected on it alone it would suffice them.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Asr (103) has three ayahs: an oath by time, the declaration that mankind is in loss, and the four exceptions — faith, righteous deeds, and mutual counsel to truth and to patience.

clues: It was a period of internal conflict.
It followed the killing of a caliph.
It fell within the caliphate of Ali.
It included the Battle of the Camel.
It also included Siffin.
hard.explain: The first fitnah was the civil conflict following the killing of Uthman, encompassing the Battle of the Camel in 36 AH and Siffin in 37 AH during Ali's caliphate.

clues: They took place immediately after the Prophet's passing.
They fell within the caliphate of Abu Bakr.
They concerned tribes withdrawing from the new state.
They included the Battle of Yamamah.
They ended with the peninsula reunified.
hard.explain: The Ridda campaigns under Abu Bakr addressed tribes that withheld allegiance or zakat after the Prophet's passing. The Battle of Yamamah was their costliest engagement.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of seventy-three ayahs.
It is surah 33.
Its name refers to a confederacy.
It relates to the siege of Madinah.
It also contains the verse naming the Prophet ﷺ as the seal of the prophets.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ahzab (33) is named for the Confederates who besieged Madinah at Khandaq. It contains 33:40, naming the Prophet ﷺ as the Seal of the Prophets.

clues: He was among the earliest Muslims.
He is one of the ten given glad tidings.
He emigrated twice, to Abyssinia and then Madinah.
He was known for great wealth and generosity.
Umar appointed him to the council that chose the next caliph.
hard.explain: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf was among the earliest Muslims and the ten promised Paradise, known for his wealth and generosity, and a member of the shura Umar appointed to select his successor.

clues: It was a council convened to make a decision.
It was set up as a caliph lay dying.
It consisted of six senior companions.
Its task was to select a successor.
Its outcome was the caliphate of Uthman.
hard.explain: Umar appointed a council of six senior companions to choose his successor from among themselves. Their deliberation resulted in the selection of Uthman.

clues: It was a gathering in Madinah.
It took place immediately after the Prophet's passing.
It was initially a meeting of the Ansar.
Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubaydah arrived during it.
It concluded with allegiance given to Abu Bakr.
hard.explain: The gathering at the Saqifah of Banu Sa'idah immediately after the Prophet's passing concluded with the pledge of allegiance to Abu Bakr as the first caliph.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of seventy-five ayahs.
It is surah 8.
Its name refers to the spoils of war.
It was revealed largely in connection with one battle.
That battle is Badr.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Anfal (8) relates largely to the Battle of Badr and its aftermath, including the distribution of spoils. It is followed by At-Tawbah, the only surah without the Basmalah.

clues: It is a traditional grouping of surahs.
It refers to the final portion of the mushaf.
Its surahs are comparatively short.
Scholars differ over exactly where it begins.
It runs to the end of the Qur'an.
hard.explain: Al-Mufassal is the final section of the mushaf, comprising the shorter surahs. Scholars differ on its starting point, commonly given as Surah Qaf or Al-Hujurat.

clues: It is a traditional grouping of surahs.
It refers to the opening portion of the mushaf.
It contains seven surahs.
It begins with Al-Baqarah.
Its seventh member is disputed.
hard.explain: Al-Sab' al-Tiwal are the seven long surahs beginning at Al-Baqarah. The seventh is counted either as Al-Anfal with At-Tawbah together, or as Yunus.

clues: He was an uncle of the Prophet ﷺ.
He raised him after the death of his grandfather.
He protected him for many years in Makkah.
He did not accept Islam, by the well-known accounts.
He died in the Year of Sorrow.
hard.explain: Abu Talib raised and protected the Prophet ﷺ through the difficult Makkan years. His death, alongside Khadijah's, gave the Year of Sorrow its name.

clues: He was a leading figure of the Quraysh.
He led opposition to the Muslims for years.
He commanded at Uhud.
He did not die in that opposition.
He accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah.
hard.explain: Abu Sufyan led Quraysh opposition for years, including at Uhud, and accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of thirteen ayahs.
It is surah 60.
Its name refers to a woman being examined.
It addresses relations with those outside the community.
It concerns the testing of women who migrated to Madinah.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60) addresses loyalty and relations with those outside the community, and the examination of women who emigrated to Madinah.

clues: It is a pair of terms in Qur'anic study.
It concerns the relationship between two texts.
One of them supersedes the other.
Scholars differ widely over how many cases exist.
It is the abrogating and the abrogated.
hard.explain: Nasikh is the abrogating text and mansukh the abrogated. Scholars broadly accept the principle but differ substantially over how many verses it affects.

clues: It is a pair of terms in Qur'anic study.
Surah Al-Imran mentions both in a single verse.
One kind is clear in meaning.
The other admits of more than one reading.
That verse warns against pursuing the second to cause discord.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Imran 3:7 distinguishes the muhkam, verses clear in meaning, from the mutashabih, those that are not, and warns against pursuing the latter to sow discord.

clues: He was a scholar of the later medieval period.
He was born in Tunis and died in 1406.
He served in several courts in North Africa and Egypt.
He is best known for one introductory work.
That work is the Muqaddimah.
hard.explain: Ibn Khaldun (d. 1406) is best known for the Muqaddimah, the introduction to his universal history, widely regarded as a foundational work in historiography and social thought.

clues: She was a wife of the Prophet ﷺ.
She had earlier migrated to Abyssinia.
She was present at Hudaybiyyah.
Her counsel there resolved a difficult moment.
She advised the Prophet ﷺ to act first and let the people follow.
hard.explain: At Hudaybiyyah, when the companions hesitated to leave ihram, Umm Salamah advised the Prophet ﷺ to perform the act himself first, after which the people followed.

options: The clause on the delayed Umrah
clues: It was a term of a written agreement.
That agreement was concluded in 6 AH.
It concerned the cessation of hostilities.
It was the term with the longest horizon.
It set a period of ten years.
hard.explain: The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah established a ten-year truce. Its other terms included the postponement of the Umrah by a year and provisions on those who crossed between the two sides.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of thirty-eight ayahs.
It is surah 47.
It is named after a person.
It is sometimes also called Surah al-Qital.
It is the only surah bearing the Prophet's name.
hard.explain: Surah Muhammad (47) is the only surah named after the Prophet ﷺ. It is also known as Surah al-Qital for its subject matter.

clues: He was a young companion from Madinah.
He served as a scribe of revelation.
He was entrusted with a task after the Prophet's passing.
He gathered the Qur'an into a written collection under Abu Bakr.

Wudu involves washing the face, arms and feet.
Wudu is performed only once a year.
easy.explain: Wudu is performed whenever it has been invalidated and prayer is to be offered — potentially several times a day.

statements: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
The Tawrat was given to Prophet Musa.
The Zabur was given to Prophet Isa.
easy.explain: The Zabur was given to Prophet Dawud. Prophet Isa was given the Injil.

statements: Hajj is performed in Dhul-Hijjah.
Umrah can be performed at any time of year.
Hajj can be performed at any time of year.
easy.explain: Hajj has a fixed season in Dhul-Hijjah. It is Umrah that may be performed at any time.

statements: Fajr is prayed before sunrise.
Maghrib is prayed after sunset.
Isha is prayed before Maghrib.
easy.explain: Isha comes after Maghrib. The order through the day is Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha.

statements: The Ka'bah is a cube-shaped structure.
Pilgrims walk around the Ka'bah seven times.
Pilgrims walk around the Ka'bah three times.
easy.explain: Tawaf consists of seven circuits around the Ka'bah.

statements: Angels are created beings.
Jibril brought revelation to the prophets.
Jibril was a prophet sent to his own people.
easy.explain: Jibril is an angel, not a prophet. Prophets are human beings chosen from among their own people.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah is recited in every rak'ah.
Surah Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs.
Surah Al-Fatihah is the last surah in the Qur'an.
easy.explain: Al-Fatihah is the first surah. The last is An-Nas, surah 114.

statements: The shahada has two parts.
Saying the shahada sincerely is how one enters Islam.
The shahada is one of the pillars of iman.
easy.explain: The shahada is the first of the five pillars of Islam. The articles of iman are a separate list of six beliefs.

statements: Prophet Nuh built an ark.
Prophet Musa was given the Tawrat.
Prophet Nuh was given the Tawrat.
easy.explain: The Tawrat was given to Musa. No scripture is named in the Qur'an as having been given to Nuh.

statements: Maryam is the mother of Prophet Isa.
Maryam is named in the Qur'an.
Maryam was a prophet.
easy.explain: Maryam is honoured as chosen above the women of the worlds, and a surah bears her name, but she is not counted among the prophets.

statements: Muslims greet one another with as-salamu alaykum.
The greeting means peace be upon you.
The greeting is only used once a year.
easy.explain: The greeting of peace is used in everyday life, whenever Muslims meet.

statements: Fasting is obligatory during Ramadan.
Children before puberty are not obliged to fast.
Everyone without exception must fast, including the seriously ill.
easy.explain: The Qur'an exempts the sick and the traveller, who make up the days later; those permanently unable to fast give fidyah instead.

statements: The Qur'an has 114 surahs.
Surah An-Nas is the last surah.
Surah An-Nas is the first surah.
easy.explain: An-Nas is surah 114, the last. Al-Fatihah is the first.

statements: Hajj takes place in Makkah.
Tawaf is performed around the Ka'bah.
Tawaf is performed around Mount Arafah.
easy.explain: Tawaf is the circling of the Ka'bah. Arafah is a plain where pilgrims stand on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah; there is no circling there.

statements: Angels are created from light, according to hadith.
Angels do not disobey Allah.
Angels are a kind of prophet.
easy.explain: Angels and prophets are entirely distinct. Prophets are human beings chosen from among people.

statements: Muslims believe in all the prophets.
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet.
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the first prophet.
easy.explain: Adam, ʿalayhi al-salām, is the first. Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet, the seal of the prophets.

statements: Salah is performed five times a day.
Each salah has a set number of rak'ahs.
Each of the five prayers has the same number of rak'ahs.
easy.explain: Fajr has two rak'ahs, Maghrib three, and Dhuhr, Asr and Isha four each.

statements: The Qur'an is the word of Allah.
It was revealed through the angel Jibril.
It was written by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself.
easy.explain: The Qur'an is revelation, not authorship. It was conveyed through Jibril, memorised and recorded by scribes among the companions.

statements: A mosque is a place of worship.
The imam leads the congregational prayer.
The imam must be an angel.
easy.explain: The imam is a person who leads the prayer; any qualified Muslim man may do so.

statements: Zakat helps those in need.
Sadaqah is voluntary.
Sadaqah is obligatory and zakat is voluntary.
easy.explain: It is the other way round: zakat is obligatory with fixed rules, while sadaqah is voluntary.

statements: Laylat al-Qadr falls in Ramadan.
Eid al-Fitr falls in Shawwal.
Laylat al-Qadr falls in Shawwal.
easy.explain: Laylat al-Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan. Shawwal is the month that follows, beginning with Eid al-Fitr.

statements: Prophet Ibrahim is associated with the Ka'bah.
Prophet Isma'il was his son.
Prophet Musa was his son.
easy.explain: Isma'il and Ishaq were sons of Ibrahim. Musa came many generations later.

statements: The adhan is the call to prayer.
It is called before each obligatory prayer.
It is called only on Fridays.
easy.explain: The adhan precedes each of the five daily prayers, every day.

statements: Muslims fast from food and drink while fasting.
The fast is broken at sunset.
The fast is broken at midnight.
easy.explain: The fast ends at sunset with iftar, at the time of the Maghrib prayer.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah opens the Qur'an.
It is recited in every rak'ah.
It has seventy ayahs.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs, not seventy.

statements: Jibril brought the first revelation.
The first revelation came at the cave of Hira.
The first revelation came in Madinah.
easy.explain: The first revelation came at the cave of Hira, near Makkah, years before the migration to Madinah.

statements: Wudu can be invalidated and then repeated.
Ghusl is a full bath required in certain states.
Ghusl and wudu are exactly the same thing.
easy.explain: Wudu is the partial ablution before prayer; ghusl is the complete washing of the body required in specific states of impurity.

statements: Believing in the angels is an article of faith.
Believing in the Last Day is an article of faith.
Believing in the five pillars is one of the six articles of faith.
easy.explain: The five pillars are acts of Islam, not items in the list of six beliefs. The six articles are Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree.

statements: Prophet Sulayman was a king as well as a prophet.
Prophet Dawud was given the Zabur.
Prophet Sulayman was given the Zabur.
easy.explain: The Zabur was given to Dawud, the father of Sulayman.

statements: Prophet Yunus was swallowed by a great fish.
Prophet Ayyub is known for his patience.
Prophet Ayyub was swallowed by a great fish.
easy.explain: That was Yunus. Ayyub is remembered for patience through severe illness and loss.

statements: Adam was the first human being.
Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet.
Adam was the final prophet.
easy.explain: Adam, ʿalayhi al-salām, was the first. Muhammad ﷺ is the seal of the prophets.

statements: The Qur'an is divided into 30 ajza.
Many people read one juz a night in Ramadan.
The Qur'an is divided into 30 surahs.
easy.explain: The Qur'an has 114 surahs. It is the juz divisions that number thirty.

statements: Jannah is the reward of the believers.
Jahannam is a place of punishment.
Jannah is a place of punishment.
easy.explain: Jannah is paradise; Jahannam is the Fire.

statements: Iblis refused to prostrate to Adam.
Iblis was of the jinn.
Iblis was one of the angels.
easy.explain: The Qur'an states explicitly that Iblis was of the jinn. Angels do not disobey what they are commanded.

statements: SubhanAllah is a phrase of remembrance.
Alhamdulillah means all praise is for Allah.
Alhamdulillah means Allah is the Greatest.
easy.explain: Allahu akbar means Allah is the Greatest. Alhamdulillah is praise.

statements: A hafiz has memorised the whole Qur'an.
The imam leads the prayer.
A hafiz is someone who leads the prayer.
easy.explain: A hafiz is a memoriser of the Qur'an. Leading the prayer is the role of the imam, though a hafiz often does so.

statements: Halal means permitted.
Haram means forbidden.
Halal means forbidden.
easy.explain: Halal is the permitted and haram the forbidden — the two are opposites.

statements: Prophet Harun was the brother of Musa.
Prophet Isma'il was a son of Ibrahim.
Prophet Harun was a son of Ibrahim.
easy.explain: Harun was the brother of Musa, many generations after Ibrahim.

statements: The mihrab shows the direction of prayer.
The minbar is used for the sermon.
The minbar shows the direction of prayer.
easy.explain: The mihrab is the niche marking the qiblah; the minbar is the pulpit.

statements: Zakat al-Fitr is given before the Eid prayer.
Zakat al-Mal is calculated on wealth.
Zakat al-Fitr is calculated on wealth.
easy.explain: Zakat al-Fitr is a fixed amount per person. Zakat al-Mal is the one calculated against wealth and the nisab.

statements: Tayammum uses clean earth.
Tayammum is used when water is unavailable.
Tayammum is performed with water.
easy.explain: Tayammum is specifically the dry alternative to wudu, used when water is unavailable or harmful.

statements: Prophet Isa was given the Injil.
Prophet Musa was given the Tawrat.
Prophet Isa was given the Tawrat.
easy.explain: The Tawrat was given to Musa and the Injil to Isa, ʿalayhim al-salām.

statements: Qiyam is the standing position in prayer.
Sujud is prostration.
Qiyam is prostration.
easy.explain: Qiyam is standing; sujud is prostration.

statements: Prophet Nuh's people were destroyed by a flood.
Prophet Nuh built an ark.
Prophet Nuh's people were destroyed by an earthquake.
easy.explain: The punishment of Nuh's people was the flood, from which those with him in the ark were saved.

statements: Istighfar is seeking forgiveness.
Takbir is saying Allahu akbar.
Istighfar is saying Allahu akbar.
easy.explain: Istighfar is seeking forgiveness, commonly Astaghfirullah. Takbir is Allahu akbar.

statements: Surah Al-Kawthar is the shortest surah.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest.
Surah Al-Kawthar is the longest surah.
easy.explain: Al-Kawthar has three ayahs; Al-Baqarah has 286.

statements: Prophet Yusuf was thrown into a well by his brothers.
A surah is named after Yusuf.
Prophet Yusuf was thrown into a well by his father.
easy.explain: It was his brothers. His father Ya'qub grieved his loss for many years.

statements: Maryam is the mother of Isa.
Surah Maryam is named after her.
Maryam is the mother of Musa.
easy.explain: Maryam is the mother of Isa, ʿalayhi al-salām.

statements: Surah Al-Balad has 20 ayat.
Surah An-Nisa was revealed in Makkah.
Surah Al-Ikhlas has 4 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah An-Nisa is a Madani surah, revealed in Madinah. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Humazah was revealed in Makkah.
Surah 'Abasa has 32 ayat.
The name Surah Al-Qadr means “The Power”.
easy.explain: Surah 'Abasa has 42 ayat, not 32. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Waqi'ah comes right after Surah At-Tur.
Surah Al-Fil comes right after Surah Al-Humazah.
Surah Ya-Sin was revealed in Makkah.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Waqi'ah comes right after Surah Ar-Rahman, not Surah At-Tur. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The name Surah An-Nas means “Mankind”.
The name Surah Al-Bayyinah means “The Clear Proof”.
Surah Al-Qari'ah was revealed in Madinah.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Qari'ah is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Kafirun was revealed in Makkah.
Surah Al-Balad has 12 ayat.
The name Surah Al-Ghashiyah means “The Overwhelming”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Balad has 20 ayat, not 12. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Quraysh comes right after Surah Al-Fil.
Surah Az-Zalzalah has 12 ayat.
The name Surah Al-Ghashiyah means “The Overwhelming”.
easy.explain: Surah Az-Zalzalah has 8 ayat, not 12. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah At-Tariq comes right after Surah Al-Balad.
Surah Al-Layl comes right after Surah Ash-Shams.
Surah Al-Waqi'ah has 96 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah At-Tariq comes right after Surah Al-Buruj, not Surah Al-Balad. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Ma'un has 7 ayat.
The name Surah Al-Fil means “Originator”.
The name Surah Al-Bayyinah means “The Clear Proof”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Fil means “The Elephant”. “Originator” is the meaning of Surah Fatir. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-'Alaq has 19 ayat.
The name Surah Al-Ghashiyah means “The Night Journey”.
The name Surah 'Abasa means “He Frowned”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Ghashiyah means “The Overwhelming”. “The Night Journey” is the meaning of Surah Al-Isra. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Yusuf was revealed in Madinah.
Surah An-Nisa has 176 ayat.
Surah Al-Kawthar comes right after Surah Al-Ma'un.
easy.explain: Surah Yusuf is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Mulk comes right after Surah At-Tahrim.
Surah Al-Layl was revealed in Madinah.
The name Surah Yusuf means “Joseph”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Layl is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-'Alaq comes right after Surah At-Tin.
Surah At-Takwir comes right after Surah An-Naba.
Surah Al-Layl was revealed in Makkah.
easy.explain: Surah At-Takwir comes right after Surah 'Abasa, not Surah An-Naba. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The name Surah Al-Fatihah means “The Emissaries”.
Surah Al-Fil comes right after Surah Al-Humazah.
The name Surah Al-Bayyinah means “The Clear Proof”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Fatihah means “The Opener”. “The Emissaries” is the meaning of Surah Al-Mursalat. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Fil was revealed in Madinah.
Surah Al-Fajr has 30 ayat.
The name Surah Al-Ikhlas means “The Sincerity”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Fil is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Ikhlas has 4 ayat.
The name Surah An-Nas means “Mankind”.
Surah Al-Kawthar has 10 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Kawthar has 3 ayat, not 10. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Ikhlas comes right after Surah Al-Falaq.
The name Surah An-Nasr means “The Divine Support”.
Surah Al-'Adiyat comes right after Surah Az-Zalzalah.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Ikhlas comes right after Surah Al-Masad, not Surah Al-Falaq. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf comes right after Surah Al-Anbya.
Surah Al-Fatihah has 7 ayat.
Surah Al-Infitar was revealed in Makkah.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Kahf comes right after Surah Al-Isra, not Surah Al-Anbya. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Az-Zalzalah has 15 ayat.
Surah At-Takwir comes right after Surah 'Abasa.
The name Surah Al-'Adiyat means “The Courser”.
easy.explain: Surah Az-Zalzalah has 8 ayat, not 15. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Inshiqaq was revealed in Makkah.
Surah Al-'Alaq comes right after Surah Ad-Duhaa.
The name Surah Al-Fatihah means “The Opener”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-'Alaq comes right after Surah At-Tin, not Surah Ad-Duhaa. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Buruj was revealed in Makkah.
Surah An-Nazi'at has 60 ayat.
Surah An-Nisa was revealed in Madinah.
easy.explain: Surah An-Nazi'at has 46 ayat, not 60. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Bayyinah comes right after Surah Al-Qadr.
Surah Al-A'la comes right after Surah Ash-Shams.
Surah An-Nas has 6 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah Al-A'la comes right after Surah At-Tariq, not Surah Ash-Shams. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Mulk comes right after Surah At-Tahrim.
Surah An-Nisa comes right after Surah Ali 'Imran.
Surah Al-Qadr comes right after Surah Al-Qari'ah.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Qadr comes right after Surah Al-'Alaq, not Surah Al-Qari'ah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Yusuf was revealed in Madinah.
The name Surah Al-Qadr means “The Power”.
The name Surah Al-'Alaq means “The Clot”.
easy.explain: Surah Yusuf is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Ali 'Imran was revealed in Madinah.
Surah Ar-Rahman has 78 ayat.
Surah Ad-Duhaa was revealed in Madinah.
easy.explain: Surah Ad-Duhaa is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah At-Takwir has 29 ayat.
Surah Quraysh comes right after Surah Al-Fil.
Surah Ash-Shams was revealed in Madinah.
easy.explain: Surah Ash-Shams is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah An-Nasr comes right after Surah Al-Kafirun.
Surah Al-Qari'ah comes right after Surah Al-Humazah.
Surah Al-Layl has 21 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Qari'ah comes right after Surah Al-'Adiyat, not Surah Al-Humazah. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Az-Zalzalah has 14 ayat.
Surah Al-Qadr has 5 ayat.
Surah Ash-Shams has 15 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah Az-Zalzalah has 8 ayat, not 14. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Ar-Rahman has 78 ayat.
The name Surah An-Nas means “The Morning Hours”.
The name Surah Al-Mutaffifin means “The Defrauding”.
easy.explain: Surah An-Nas means “Mankind”. “The Morning Hours” is the meaning of Surah Ad-Duhaa. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: The name Surah Al-Mulk means “The Sovereignty”.
Surah Al-Fatihah has 7 ayat.
The name Surah Al-'Adiyat means “The Prohibition”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-'Adiyat means “The Courser”. “The Prohibition” is the meaning of Surah At-Tahrim. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Az-Zalzalah has 12 ayat.
Surah An-Naba comes right after Surah Al-Mursalat.
Surah Maryam was revealed in Makkah.
easy.explain: Surah Az-Zalzalah has 8 ayat, not 12. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Maryam comes right after Surah Al-Kahf.
The name Surah Al-Falaq means “The Daybreak”.
Surah Al-A'la comes right after Surah Al-Balad.
easy.explain: Surah Al-A'la comes right after Surah At-Tariq, not Surah Al-Balad. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The name Surah An-Nasr means “The Divine Support”.
Surah Quraysh was revealed in Madinah.
Surah Al-Waqi'ah has 96 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah Quraysh is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: The name Surah Al-Mutaffifin means “The Defrauding”.
Surah Al-Qari'ah comes right after Surah Al-'Adiyat.
Surah Al-Kawthar has 8 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Kawthar has 3 ayat, not 8. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Ash-Shams comes right after Surah At-Tin.
The name Surah Maryam means “Mary”.
Surah Al-Ma'un comes right after Surah Quraysh.
easy.explain: Surah Ash-Shams comes right after Surah Al-Balad, not Surah At-Tin. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Ma'un comes right after Surah Quraysh.
Surah 'Abasa has 30 ayat.
Surah Al-Ghashiyah comes right after Surah Al-A'la.
easy.explain: Surah 'Abasa has 42 ayat, not 30. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah An-Naba has 33 ayat.
Surah Ya-Sin comes right after Surah Fatir.
The name Surah Al-Qari'ah means “The Calamity”.
easy.explain: Surah An-Naba has 40 ayat, not 33. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Baqarah was revealed in Madinah.
The name Surah Al-Waqi'ah means “The Rooms”.
Surah Quraysh comes right after Surah Al-Fil.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Waqi'ah means “The Inevitable”. “The Rooms” is the meaning of Surah Al-Hujurat. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf was revealed in Madinah.
Surah Al-Buruj has 22 ayat.
Surah Al-Infitar comes right after Surah At-Takwir.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Kahf is a Makki surah, revealed in Makkah. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Ma'un has 7 ayat.
The name Surah 'Abasa means “He Frowned”.
Surah Al-'Adiyat has 19 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah Al-'Adiyat has 11 ayat, not 19. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Al-Kafirun comes right after Surah Al-Kawthar.
The name Surah Ash-Sharh means “The Disbelievers”.
Surah Al-Infitar comes right after Surah At-Takwir.
easy.explain: Surah Ash-Sharh means “The Relief”. “The Disbelievers” is the meaning of Surah Al-Kafirun. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The name Surah At-Takwir means “The Overthrowing”.
Surah At-Tariq was revealed in Makkah.
Surah Al-Fajr comes right after Surah At-Tariq.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Fajr comes right after Surah Al-Ghashiyah, not Surah At-Tariq. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Ad-Duhaa comes right after Surah Al-Layl.
Surah Al-Fajr has 30 ayat.
The name Surah Al-A'la means “The Believers”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-A'la means “The Most High”. “The Believers” is the meaning of Surah Al-Mu'minun. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: The name Surah Al-A'la means “The Most High”.
Surah An-Naba was revealed in Makkah.
Surah Al-Baqarah has 333 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 ayat, not 333. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: The name Surah Ad-Duhaa means “The Morning Hours”.
The name Surah Ash-Shams means “The Sun”.
The name Surah Ar-Rahman means “The Troops”.
easy.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman means “The Beneficent”. “The Troops” is the meaning of Surah Az-Zumar. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Baqarah has 238 ayat.
Surah Al-Kahf has 110 ayat.
The name Surah Yusuf means “Joseph”.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 ayat, not 238. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: The name Surah Al-Kahf means “The Cave”.
The name Surah Al-Balad means “The City”.
Surah Al-Buruj has 26 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Buruj has 22 ayat, not 26. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah Ali 'Imran comes right after Surah Al-Baqarah.
Surah Maryam comes right after Surah Al-Kahf.
The name Surah Ar-Rahman means “The Ant”.
easy.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman means “The Beneficent”. “The Ant” is the meaning of Surah An-Naml. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Al-Fajr comes right after Surah Al-Ghashiyah.
Surah Al-'Asr has 7 ayat.
Surah Al-Masad has 5 ayat.
easy.explain: Surah Al-'Asr has 3 ayat, not 7. The other two statements are correct. Ayat counts follow the standard Hafs mushaf.

statements: Surah At-Tariq comes right after Surah Al-Buruj.
The name Surah Al-Masad means “The Night Journey”.
Surah At-Takathur comes right after Surah Al-Qari'ah.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Masad means “The Palm Fiber”. “The Night Journey” is the meaning of Surah Al-Isra. The other two statements are correct.

statements: The name Surah At-Takathur means “The Poets”.
Surah Al-'Asr was revealed in Makkah.
Surah Ali 'Imran comes right after Surah Al-Baqarah.
easy.explain: Surah At-Takathur means “Rivalry in increase”. “The Poets” is the meaning of Surah Ash-Shu'ara. The other two statements are correct.

statements: Surah Ali 'Imran was revealed in Makkah.
Surah Al-Infitar comes right after Surah At-Takwir.
Surah An-Nasr comes right after Surah Al-Kafirun.

The Prophet's ring was engraved with his date of birth.
hard.explain: He had a silver ring engraved Muhammad Rasul Allah. The other two statements are correct.

events.text: The first revelation at the cave of Hira

easy.explain: The first revelation came around 610 CE. The migration to Madinah followed about twelve years later, in 622 CE.

events.text: The birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was born around 570 CE. Makkah was conquered peacefully in 8 AH, 630 CE, around sixty years later.
The Hijrah was in 622 CE and the Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH, 632 CE, shortly before the Prophet ﷺ passed away.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Badr was fought in 2 AH, 624 CE. The Prophet ﷺ passed away in 11 AH, 632 CE.
The Year of the Elephant is traditionally placed around the year of the Prophet's birth, about forty years before the first revelation.

events.text: The first revelation at the cave of Hira

easy.explain: Revelation began around 610 CE. Makkah was entered peacefully twenty years later, in 8 AH.
Masjid Quba was built on arrival in Madinah at the very start of the Madinan period. The Farewell Pilgrimage came nine years later, shortly before the Prophet's passing.

events.text: The Prophet ﷺ receives his first revelation
The Prophet ﷺ passes away in Madinah

easy.explain: Around twenty-two years separate the first revelation from the Prophet's passing in Madinah.

events.text: The caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan begins

easy.explain: Badr was fought in the second year after the Hijrah; Uthman became caliph twenty-one years later.
A group of Muslims first sought refuge in Abyssinia around 615 CE, some seven years before the migration to Madinah.

events.text: The birth of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was around fifty-two at the time of the Hijrah.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins

easy.explain: Hudaybiyyah came five years before the Prophet's passing and the accession of Abu Bakr.
The Year of the Elephant is traditionally placed around the Prophet's birth, some fifty-four years before Badr.
Around seventeen years passed between the start of public preaching in Makkah and the city's peaceful conquest.

events.text: The change of qiblah to the Ka'bah

easy.explain: The qiblah was changed early in the Madinan period; Tabuk was the last major expedition, seven years later.
The Prophet ﷺ married Khadijah around fifteen years before the first revelation came to him at the cave of Hira.
The Prophet ﷺ was about thirty-five when he settled the Quraysh dispute over placing the Black Stone, some seventeen years before the Hijrah.
The night journey took place in the final Makkan years, about a decade before Makkah was entered peacefully.

Thirty-four years separate the migration from the beginning of Ali's caliphate.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Abu Bakr and Umar led in the twelve years between the Prophet's passing and Uthman's accession.
About eighteen years separate the beginning of revelation from the truce at Hudaybiyyah.

events.text: The boycott of Banu Hashim begins

easy.explain: The Makkan boycott preceded the Hijrah; Badr was fought two years after the migration.
The Prophet ﷺ was around forty-three when the call became public, three years after the first revelation.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins

easy.explain: Three years separate the conquest of Makkah from the Prophet's passing and Abu Bakr's accession.
Five years separate Badr from Khaybar, which followed the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

events.text: The caliphate of Hasan ibn Ali

events.text: The Prophet ﷺ is orphaned of his mother Aminah

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ lost his mother at about six years of age, some thirty-four years before revelation began.

events.text: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib accepts Islam

easy.explain: Hamza accepted Islam during the Makkan years and was killed at Uhud, about nine years later.

events.text: Bilal ibn Rabah is persecuted in Makkah
Bilal gives the adhan at the conquest of Makkah

easy.explain: Bilal was tortured for his faith in Makkah and later called the adhan from atop the Ka'bah when the city was taken.

events.text: The Muslims are commanded to face Jerusalem in prayer
The qiblah is changed to the Ka'bah

easy.explain: Jerusalem was the first qiblah; the direction was changed to the Ka'bah in the second year after the Hijrah.

events.text: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib leads the migrants in Abyssinia

easy.explain: Ja'far spoke for the Muslims before the Negus in Abyssinia and was killed years later at Mu'tah.

events.text: Salman al-Farisi suggests digging a trench

easy.explain: Salman's suggestion shaped the defence of Madinah at Khandaq, three years before Makkah was entered.

events.text: Mus'ab ibn Umayr is sent to teach in Yathrib

easy.explain: Mus'ab was sent to Yathrib after the first Pledge of Aqabah and was killed at Uhud a few years later.

easy.explain: Khalid fought against the Muslims at Uhud, accepted Islam before the conquest of Makkah, and later commanded at Yarmuk.
